candidates.name: Bratislava Castle
candidates.content: The castle contains a Museum of Bratislava History, and a baroque garden. There is also a restaurant open till after the actual castle tours into the night. The general precinct area immediately outside the castle, including the v

candidates.name: Danubiana Meulensteen Art Museum
candidates.content: If you like modern art better, pay a visit to the Danubiana Art Museum on the southern edge of Bratislava. It is about 20km from the city center, so too far to walk. Take bus nr 90 from the National Theater, a taxi, or drive. It i

candidates.name: Museum of Transport
candidates.price: Adults €8, students and seniors 65-70 €4, children 3-6 and seniors 70+ €1, children under 3 free. Free entry on first Wednesday of each month
candidates.content: With a display of historical vehicles (automobiles, farm vehicles, bicycles, firefighting vehicles, railway, model ships and model buses) in the first railway station in the city, very close to the current Main Railway Station. Fr

candidates.name: St. Martin's Cathedral
candidates.content: The largest and one of the oldest churches in Bratislava, situated below Bratislava Castle. The Gothic cathedral, formerly the coronation-church of several Hungarian kings, begun in 1204, and reconsecrated in 1445, was restored in

candidates.name: SNP Bridge
candidates.alt: Most Slovenského národného povstania, called Nový most from 1993 to 2012
candidates.price: Entrance €6.50, but is free of charge if you eat in the restaurant
candidates.content: A bridge over the Danube river, with its flying saucer-shaped structure housing a restaurant called "UFO". There is an observation deck on its roof, open from 10:00-23:00 daily, offering great views of the old town, as well as the

candidates.name: Slovak National Gallery (SNG)
candidates.content: For a taste of visual arts, pay a visit to the National Gallery at the embankment between Starý most and Nový most with permanent collections of Slovak and European medieval art pieces, although the temporary exhibitions tend to b

candidates.name: Bratislava City Gallery (GMB)
candidates.content: Bratislava City Gallery is also a good pick to see displays of historical fine arts, paintings and sculptures along with interesting temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Mirbach Palace
candidates.content: Rococo Palace built 1768–1770. Today it hosts the Bratislava City Gallery.

candidates.name: Slavín monument
candidates.content: On the top of the hill behind the castle, overlooking the entire city. This is a monument in memory of Soviet casualties in the liberation battle of Bratislava in World War II. It is the highest place in the city, and thus the bes

candidates.name: Church of St. Elisabeth
candidates.content: Nicknamed the Blue Church (Modrý kostolík), this is a beautiful Jugendstil church finished in 1913.

candidates.name: Primate's Palace
candidates.content: Now the seat of the Mayor of Bratislava.

candidates.name: Gerulata
candidates.content: This is an ancient Roman military camp with archeological findings on display. If you're into all things Roman, you should also consider a visit to the nearby Carnuntum which has a large archeological site and is a few minutes by

candidates.name: Devín Castle
candidates.price: €8 April to October, €6 November to March
candidates.content: There has been a fortress on this site since Roman times. In the 19th and early 20th century it became a Slovak national symbol. During the Communist dictatorship, it was part of the border zone which prevented people from escapin

candidates.name: Slovak Radio Building
candidates.content: Its main building is a peculiar 60-m-high reversed pyramid from the communist era and a landmark in sharp contrast with the building of the Slovak National Bank just across the street.

candidates.name: Michael's Gate with Tower
candidates.content: This 51-m-high tower above the gate with its green copper roof is one of the best known and the oldest buildings in Bratislava. It was built in the 14th century as one of the four gates to the city.

candidates.name: Bratislava Card
candidates.price: With unlimited public transportation: €30 for 24 hr, €36 for 48 hr, €39 for 72 hr. Without public transportation: €27 for 24 hr, €32 for 48 hr, €35 for 72 hr
candidates.content: This is very good value, particularly if visiting for more than 24 hours. You can purchase either a physical or digital card. Available for 24, 48 or 72 hrs. Time starts when you first use the physical card or activates the digita

candidates.name: Natural Science Museum
candidates.content: Echoing the communist era, the natural science exhibitions have an interesting collection of artifacts and is slowly being transformed into a modern era exhibition.

candidates.name: Jewish Community Museum
candidates.content: Rare Jewish ritual tools, gold-embroidered mantles protecting the holy biblical scrolls, unique photographs of students who had attended the famed Bratislava rabbi school that reveal even to this day the atrocities of the Holocaus

candidates.name: Museum of City History
candidates.content: Including the museums of history and music as well as the city dungeon and the exhibition on medieval justice.

candidates.name: Old Town Hall
candidates.content: The Old Town Hall and Apponyi Palace is open to the public as a museum, with an exhibition of city history.

candidates.name: Grassalkovich Palace and gardens
candidates.content: Also known as the Presidential Palace (Prezidentský palác) - a Rococo/late Baroque summer palace with a French garden, used as a seat of the President of Slovakia. In one of the garden's alleys you will see a row of trees planted

candidates.name: Gallery Nedbalka
candidates.content: Gallery of modern Slovak art from the late 19th century, in a building reminiscent of the New York Guggenheim.

candidates.name: Palffy Palace
candidates.content: Rebuilt in the classical style in the 19th century by Count John Pálffy. Part of the Bratislava City Gallery.

candidates.name: International Film Festival Bratislava
candidates.content: Forever in December.

candidates.name: Speedboats.sk
candidates.content: Enjoy the beautiful view of Bratislava and the surrounding nature of the river Danube during a Bratislava boat trip.

candidates.name: The Uprising Music Festival
candidates.content: Smaller multigenre music festival. Yearly in the end of August in Bratislava.

candidates.name: UFO
candidates.content: If you want to go for extraordinary, visit UFO. It looks like a cliché flying saucer and it's a high on the SNP Bridge (the member of great-towers.com), and you have to use a lift to go there. There is a good restaurant and lounge

candidates.name: ruido.cafe
candidates.content: Gay bar.

candidates.name: Apollon Gay Club
candidates.content: Gay bar.

candidates.name: Slovak Pub
candidates.content: For good and reasonably priced halušky, the unique Slovak national meal, visit the Slovak Pub on Obchodna. This is a traditional eatery with a nice ambience. Portion size leans towards the small side. Not wheelchair accessible.

candidates.name: UFO
candidates.content: You can get a nice view and can meet some local celebrities at the übercool and very expensive UFO restaurant and disco on top of Nový most bridge.

candidates.name: Flagship
candidates.content: Slovak national cuisine including halušky, in a converted theatre. Lacklustre service. Same company as Slovak Pub, who also own brewery Kláštorný pivovar, and café Franz Xaver Messerschmidt next door.

candidates.name: ECK
candidates.content: Regarded as one of the best restaurants in Slovakia, bookings open two months in advance and sell out almost immediately.

candidates.name: Góvinda reštaurácia
candidates.content: Hare Krishna-operated restaurant popular with vegans and very affordable.

candidates.name: KGB Krčma Gurmánov Bratislavy
candidates.content: Communism-themed pub with high-quality beers and affordable prices.

candidates.name: U Sedliaka
candidates.content: Good typical Slovak dishes and great background music. Nice atmosphere at affordable price.

candidates.name: Olive Tree
candidates.content: Good selection of Slovac cuisine

candidates.name: Divný Janko Reštaurácia
candidates.content: Slovak and international dishes in a nice, retro ambience, the only downside is that the staff can be rude.

candidates.name: San Marten
candidates.content: San Marten is an Italian restaurant with great food and excellent service at affordable prices.

candidates.name: Bistro SOHO
candidates.content: Asian fusion cuisine.

candidates.name: Mille Baci
candidates.content: Italian restaurant specializing in dishes from Veneto.

december.text: right|thumb|Main Square during the New Year's Eve celebration, 2006

In December, be sure to indulge in the scents and flavours of the traditional Christmas Market in front of Old Town Hall and on the Hlavné námestie (main square). The market - compared to the ones in Prague and Vienna - is smaller, but has a much friendlier, almost family-like atmosphere and feels much more traditional

Adventure sports: A popular activity among locals and tourists especially during a stag party is target shooting in Bratislava. For some extreme adventure in the pure nature Slovaks and visitors can try to sail the river Small Danube in a canoe. Water sports in general are among the most beloved sports activities with

In December, don't miss the Christmas market in front of the Old Town Hall.
